summary: Proceed, with four required edits. The run's measurable part is SOURCE A (c320 at full decode_1, about +0.85% headline, same as combination 1). The neighbour conjecture can only be read from in-process gate prints, so pass 2 of band 2 must time the master-pre pair and the tiled-pre pair head to head, and band 2 must keep master's 1.05x-vs-Triton rule. The skF re-gate is noise by construction: drop it, or keep it as print-only and remove it from the confirm/refute criteria.
justification: SOURCE A is well supported: job 8d4771fe measured 19.49 us against master's two-level 22.40/22.53 us on the same row, and GATE A (cold-L2 interleaved replay, route at <= 0.98) protects it. SOURCE B is supported only where it was measured. In c2ebf6ed the tiled kernel ran 2.1 us at sliding verify_16 (128 tokens) and 2.8 us at verify_32 (256 tokens) against master's 2.8/4.2 us. It lost or was flat at 8 tokens and at sliding decode_1. Master's untiled kernel is already only 1.9-2.4 us at 16-32 tokens (judged profile: full decode_16 2.2, sliding decode_32 1.9, full decode_32 2.4). The tiled kernel cannot go much below about 1.3-1.5 us because of launch and latency cost, so the realistic saving at 16-32 tokens is 0-0.5 us. WEAKEST LINK: the claim that band 2 (sliding decode B=16) will route. The 1.006x it starts from is source E's pass-1 first-pass MINIMUM (16.2 vs 16.3 us net, a biased number per master's own comment), not a pass-2 head-to-head. To reach master's real rule for a Triton incumbent (1.05x, `need = 1.05` in _sd_gate_band), the pair must fall to about 15.5 us net, a saving of about 0.7 us. That is more than the whole plausible tiled saving at 16 tokens. Even the hypothesis's own 1.03x needs about 0.4 us. The predicted outcome is therefore 'band 2 declines', which is a fine refutation, but the expected 'faster' on sliding decode_16 is optimistic. The hypothesis also quietly changes band 2's threshold from master's 1.05x (Triton incumbent) to 1.03x. A route at 1.03-1.05 would then come from the threshold, not from the neighbour. Classes that cannot route by construction: GATE B uses a whole-step ratio <= 0.98. FD16/FD32 whole steps are 111/228 us with a 2.2/2.4 us pre node, so even a zero-cost pre node gives at best 0.980/0.989. FV16/FV32 (163/302 us, pre 2.8/4.2) are the same. Those four classes can never route, so the skF re-gate at B=16/32 always runs on master's unchanged separate pre-attention and only re-times identical code. Even if FD32 did route, the shift would be about 0.4 us on a 228 us denominator, about 0.002 in the ratio. That is below the gate's own repeatability (B=16 has read 0.988-0.996 across runs) and far below the about 6% judged-row drift, so it is not an interaction test. SD32 is the one pair class with a real chance: about 0.39 us is needed on a 19.5 us gate-net pair whose pre node is 4.0 us net in the gate. Headline readout: c320 adds about +0.85% and everything else is at most about 0.3%, all inside the ±1.5% CI. The run therefore cannot be told apart from combination 1 on headline, and judged decode_16/32 rows (0.3-0.5 us of 15.5-17.7 us, 2-3%) sit inside the ~6% row drift. The only interpretable readouts are (1) whether c320 routes and the full decode_1 row moves 22.4 -> ~19.5 us, which is outside drift, (2) the GATE B per-class pre-node lines, (3) band 2's pass-2 ratio, and (4) which kernel names appear in the judged decode_16/32 profiles. Import budget: master's 252abb7f ran 470 s from start to finish, tests and timing included, so import is somewhat less than that and the +100 s fits the 15 minutes. The 420 s skip clock is a real risk: the band-2 phase, which carries the conjecture, comes late and could be skipped. Every phase should print its elapsed IMPORT_T0 time so a skip is visible.
confounders: restack-sliding-decode-sk-window-on-cluster-master (master 7e12891): owns _sd_gate_band and its threshold rule (1.03 vs cluster, 1.05 vs Triton). Band 2 at 1.03 vs Triton is a threshold change, so a band-2 route between 1.03x and 1.05x would come from the threshold, not the tiled neighbour, unless the master-pre pair is timed in the same pass.

sliding-decode-sk-window-route (source E, unlanded B=16 numbers): the 1.006x baseline is a pass-1 biased minimum from another build. Comparing a new pass-2 number with it mixes measurement method with the change. The comparison must be made in-pass.

restack-sk-pseudo-cluster-plus-v3-fused-preattn (FUSED_PRE / skF): the skF re-gate can only shift if GATE B routes FD16/FD32, which the 0.98 whole-step rule makes impossible (pre node is 2.0%/1.1% of the step). The re-gate is a re-measurement of master and its 'margin shift' readout is noise.

full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket: the incumbent c320 must beat at full decode_1. GATE A times against the real <4,true,true> grid-SM pair, so it is not confounded, provided the comparison graph includes master's pre-attention, as stated.

paired-heads-launch-cleanup / -ab-tune-batch-gate: the pre-attention kernel writes the paired q layout on full verify at B>1. The tiled kernel must reproduce that layout byte-exactly for FV16/FV32, but those classes cannot route anyway (see above). Byte-exactness against master's paired kernel is still required for any class that does route.

fused-preattention-triton (the _pre_attention_kernel itself): source B's tiled kernel replaces it. Exactness against it (byte/ulp, cache rows) is GATE B's correctness gate, so no hidden numerical confound.
interference: No scored companion is warranted. The natural control already exists: combination 1 (combo-naive-c320-fd1-tiled-preattn-verify, queued) carries the identical SOURCE A and keeps master on the pair classes. Rows that differ between the two runs are the designed readout. An extra scored run would only add another sample inside the ~6% row drift. The interaction test does need to be self-contained in THIS run's import, at no extra cost: (1) In band 2's pass 2, time FOUR graphs interleaved in the same set: Triton, [master pre + sk p8], [tiled pre + sk p8], and the two pre nodes alone. Print Triton / pair for BOTH pairs. The difference between the two ratios IS the neighbour effect, measured in one pass with no drift. Do the same for band 3 (SD32) against cluster C=4. (2) Keep master's 1.05x rule against a Triton incumbent for band 2. If 1.03 is kept, the master-pre pair line from (1) is mandatory and the route reason must say whether the master-pre pair also cleared it. (3) Drop the skF re-gate. FD16/FD32/FV16/FV32 cannot route under GATE B's whole-step <= 0.98 rule (best case 0.980/0.989 even at zero pre cost), so the re-gate re-times master. Optionally keep the FD/FV GATE B lines as print-only diagnostics of the pre node at 16/32/128/256 tokens, which do answer the 'untested premise'. (4) Run band 2 BEFORE any optional diagnostics, and print elapsed IMPORT_T0 at every phase boundary, so a 420 s skip is visible and cannot be mistaken for a refutation.
rules_flags: None blocking. No per-call mutable or global flag state is used: TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST is set and restored at import only, which is acceptable. No BLAS-backend toggle is involved.

Band 2 is gated at B=16 x 80000 but routes the whole B=2..16 band, including small-ctx test shapes (e.g. batch 3, ctx 2047; batch 5, ctx 5000 verify). Correctness rests on master's _sd_validate cases (B=3 lens 1/2047/80000, B=16 ragged), which already cover TOK=1 kernels. Make sure the tiled-pre variant of _sd_run is also run through those same validate cases, not only the B=16 replay.

Route tables (_SD_ROUTE, the GATE B per-class table, the c320 bool) must be frozen into MappingProxyType or module bools only after every added phase completes or is skipped. A phase that passes its deadline mid-way must not leave a partially filled table. Write to a local dict and publish atomically.

c320 workspaces are torch.empty per call, sized by page_table.shape[1] and batch: shape-only, which is allowed. Confirm there is no tickets buffer or static device pointer in the new muse_full_decode_c320 module, given the two-state rotation.
open_questions: How long does master's import take on the judge? 252abb7f is 470 s for the whole run including tests and timing. If import is already ~380 s, the 420 s clock will skip band 2 and the conjecture goes untested while still spending a scored submit. Consider building c320 in parallel or early (it is independent of master's gates) only if that does not change master's measured selectors.

Was source E's band-2 1.006x ever a pass-2 number? The log shows only pass-1 lines for B=16 (grid 128 p8 at 16.2 us net). If pass 2 at B=16 has never been measured, the 'starting point' of the conjecture is unknown.

Is the tiled kernel's program count at 16-32 tokens (64 programs of 4 warps, per the conjecture) actually fewer and faster than 288-576 one-warp programs, or does it under-fill 132 SMs at that size? The GATE B SD16/SD32 pre-node lines answer this and should be printed even when the class declines.
